A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Generative Human Geometry Distribution. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction experiments, THuman2 generation results, 4DDress pose-generation examples, ablations, and a 25-participant user study.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative reconstruction, body-shape variation, interpolation, and texturing demonstrations.

M1.justification: The core flow-matching formulation, auto-decoder, and generative networks remain unchanged. v4 adds latent-space interpolation as an alternative generation procedure in Section 9.5 and a downstream texturing pipeline using depth-conditioned Wan2.1 images followed by Gaussian Splatting color optimization in Figure 21.

E1.justification: THuman2, 4DDress, and the two main generation tasks are retained. v4 adds demonstrations of controlled SMPL body-shape/gender variation, identity/garment interpolation, and texture synthesis. Loose clothing and extreme poses were already covered in v3.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Tables 2–5 and the corresponding qualitative comparisons, including ENARF, GNARF, EVA3D, E3Gen, GetAvatar, and gDNA. The newly cited Gaussian3Diff is discussed only as related work.

E3.justification: Figure 17 adds a controlled testing procedure that holds the identity feature map fixed while varying SMPL body shape and gender. Existing protocols retain the 30,000-iteration formulation comparison, 25,000-image FID evaluation, and user study with 25 participants rating two identities under eight poses.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and pose tests, v4 substantially broadens supplementary analysis through controlled body-shape/gender variation, latent interpolation, and challenging reconstruction examples with Poisson surface reconstruction. Figures 15–19 examine additional questions about generalization, latent behavior, and surface usability, although the evidence is qualitative.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The numerical tables and convergence curves retain the same reporting practices without added uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and Figure 11 are unchanged, including the method's FID of 16.16 and user-study quality/plausibility scores of 4.04/4.36. v4 adds qualitative outputs for fully trained reconstruction, challenging surfaces, body-shape variation, interpolation, and texturing in Figures 14–19 and 21; these supplement the existing results without establishing new numerical performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, nearest-neighbor pair construction, and distribution normalization retain the same mathematical content. The new appendix discussion introduces no additional formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions, two main tasks, novelty positioning, and performance claims. The appendix demonstrations do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 9.4 adds an explicit explanation of why SMPL conditioning does not confine generated clothing and hair to the template, linking generalization to displacement modeling. Figure 17 qualifies gender changes as mainly body-shape variations when identity features remain fixed, while Figure 15 discusses local sparsity in extreme cases. Section 6's existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 identifies Poisson reconstruction for Figure 15 and the Wan2.1/Gaussian Splatting procedure for Figure 21, while Figure 20 explicitly illustrates the SMPL UV parameterization. Existing feature-map dimensions, optimizer settings, hardware, training times, and memory figures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 and the bibliography add Gaussian3Diff by Lan et al. (2024), describing diffusion-based head representation learning as an alternative to GAN-based approaches. The surrounding related-work coverage and central research positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v4 adds brief representation-capability and interpolation subsections, numbers the appendix sections, adds acknowledgements, and updates author contact and corresponding-author information.

P2.justification: v4 retains Figures 1–13 and all five tables, while adding Figures 14–21. The new multipanel reconstruction, shape-variation, interpolation, and texture displays, together with the UV diagram, substantially expand the visual exposition and reorganize the appendix layout.

improvement.justification: The new appendix makes body-shape control, latent interpolation, challenging reconstructions, and downstream surface/texturing uses directly inspectable, while clarifying the representation's relationship to SMPL. These are useful additions to v3's evidence, but they remain qualitative and briefly documented; the main quantitative comparisons and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.
